Get rows of a dataset

Source: R/rows.R
gcd_rows.Rd

The core function: the rows of one dataset at one detail level, as a tibble typed from the dataset's schema, with place names beside their codes.

It returns every category and group the filters don't exclude. Nothing is pinned by default: no single demographic group, no single subject. A call with only a dataset name returns the whole dataset at its default detail level.

Usage

gcd_rows(
  name,
  ...,
  year = NULL,
  detail = NULL,
  district = NULL,
  school = NULL,
  county = NULL,
  labels = TRUE,
  columns = NULL,
  sort = NULL,
  n_max = Inf,
  cache = getOption("gcd.cache", FALSE),
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

name

The dataset's name, such as "graduation_rate_4_year_cohort" (see gcd_datasets() and gcd_search()).

...

Named filters (see "Filters"). Unnamed arguments are an error.

year

Years to keep, an integer vector. A run of consecutive years (2019:2024) is sent as a range; anything else (c(2019, 2024)) as exact years. Default NULL: all years.

detail

The one level the rows describe, such as "schools", "districts", "states", "counties" or "tracts". Default NULL: the dataset's default (the finest level, except Census datasets, which default to counties). To combine levels, call once per level and bind the rows.

district, school, county

Places by name, such as district = "Fulton County", school = "Roswell High School", county = c("Fulton", "DeKalb"). Matched exactly against current and former names (ignoring case, accents and a trailing "County"); an unknown or ambiguous name is an error that lists suggestions or candidates. A school name found in more than one district needs district too. For any one place, give its code or its name, not both. Default NULL.

labels

TRUE (default) adds place names beside codes; FALSE returns codes only (see "Labels").

columns

A character vector to return only some columns. Default NULL: all.

sort

A character vector of columns to sort by on the server; prefix - for descending ("-graduation_rate"). Missing values sort last. Mostly useful with n_max for a top N. Default NULL: the dataset's own order (its grain).

n_max

The most rows to return. Default Inf: all.

cache

TRUE to use the disk cache (see "Large downloads and the disk cache"). Default getOption("gcd.cache", FALSE).

quiet

TRUE to silence the advisory messages. Default FALSE.

Value

A tibble of rows at one detail level, typed from the schema: codes and names character (leading zeros kept), year integer, counts integer, rates and proportions double (proportions on the 0-1 scale), booleans logical. Columns come in grain order: year, each geography code followed by its names, demographic and its labels, other categorical columns, then metrics. gcd_columns() describes each column. The tibble carries a gcd_meta attribute (see gcd_meta()): dataset, title, detail, key metric, units, null_semantics, source, citation, license, advisories, data version, updated_at and the request URL.

Filters

Give filters as named arguments in ...; each value is a vector. Values within one filter are OR'd; different filters are AND'd. Accepted names:

  • any categorical column: subject = "mathematics", demographic = c("all", "black");

  • geography codes: district_code, school_code, county_fips, tract_geoid, block_group_geoid;

  • school_id: schools as "DISTRICT-SCHOOL" codes (school_id = c("761-0199", "660-0104")), the form gcd_locate() returns (a school code alone is not unique across districts);

  • lookup-table attributes: district_type = "state_charter", school_level = "high", locale = "rural", demographic_category = "race";

  • metric bounds: graduation_rate_min = 0.9, num_cohort_max = 50 (inclusive, in stored units).

NA in a filter selects rows where a nullable column is empty; logicals become true / false. The API validates every filter and its errors name what went wrong; gcd_describe() lists each dataset's filters and their values.

Labels

With labels = TRUE (the default) the rows carry the API's joined name columns, each right after its code: district_name, district_census_id and district_type after district_code; school_name after school_code; county_name, tract_name and block_group_name after their codes; demographic_label and demographic_category after demographic. Codes are always kept: school names repeat across districts, names change over time, and joins run on codes.

  • Categorical values (subject, grade_cluster) are readable snake_case codes already; there are no separate labels for them.

  • demographic_category (race, gender, economic_status, ...) is a grouping that arrives with the labels; filtering by it works either way.

  • Other lookup-table attributes (school addresses, locale, coordinates) are not joined; get them from gcd_dimension() and join.

labels = FALSE asks for the dataset's own columns only, for large pulls. gcd_columns() takes the same argument and lists the name columns too, with role "label". Either way, code columns that would be empty on every row (a district row's school_code, a state row's geography codes) are left out, so both settings give the same shape.

Missing values and totals

NA in a metric usually means the value was suppressed to protect privacy (small counts), not zero; the schema's null_semantics says which (gcd_describe()). Because nothing is pinned, results hold the all totals beside the subgroups: never add a total to its subgroups. The API's advisories say so when they apply, and print once per call as messages (quiet = TRUE or options(gcd.quiet = TRUE) silences them; they stay in gcd_meta(x)$advisories).

Rates must be pooled from their counts, never averaged: sum(num_graduates) / sum(num_cohort), not mean(graduation_rate). gcd_columns() shows each metric's numerator and denominator.

Large downloads and the disk cache

Up to 10,000 rows come back as one JSON page. A larger result is downloaded in full as CSV in one response (with a progress bar); the metadata and advisories then come from the first JSON page and describe its first 10,000 rows.

With cache = TRUE (or options(gcd.cache = TRUE)), responses are kept in tools::R_user_dir("georgiacivicdata", "cache") with their ETag. Repeating a request asks the server whether the data changed: an unchanged answer reuses the saved copy without downloading, and a new data release downloads afresh. A response the server marks fresh (for five minutes) is reused without asking. Clear it with gcd_cache_clear().

Data license

The data is CC BY 4.0: credit Georgia Civic Data and the original source, as gcd_citation() writes.

See also

gcd_values() to see which category values exist under a filter; gcd_describe() and gcd_columns() to understand a dataset; gcd_citation() to cite it.

Other get data: gcd_values()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# Names and codes (the default), one district by name
grad <- gcd_rows(
  "graduation_rate_4_year_cohort",
  district = "Fulton County",
  demographic = c("all", "black", "hispanic"),
  year = 2020:2024
)

# One school, by name within its district
gcd_rows("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort",
         district = "Fulton County", school = "Roswell High School",
         demographic = "all")

# Statewide schools, one subject, codes only
gcd_rows("ccrpi_content_mastery", year = 2025, detail = "schools",
         grade_cluster = "high", subject = "mathematics", labels = FALSE)

# Top 10 counties by unemployment
gcd_rows("employment", year = 2024, sort = "-unemployment_rate",
         n_max = 10)
}
